The requested level (write) exceeds the maximum, so the granted level is read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this. The employee Edward Fleming (E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Notes 1-5 say he's a full-time Payroll Specialist, recommend write.
Note 6 (from Security DB) says he's a contractor with basic security training, recommend read.

Conflict: employment type. The Security agent looked it up in their own database, while others either looked up role or just noted full-time from other notes. Note 1 says full_time looked up in own database. Note 2-5 didn't look up employment type; they relied on note 1.

The Security note claims the other notes assumed full-time, but Security DB shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors get read max unless advanced training. So grant max read.

Policy: If requested level is above the maximum, grant the maximum. Requested write, max read → grant read.

The key evidence: Security DB is the authoritative source for employment type (they looked it up). The others didn't look up employment type, except note 1 which says they looked it up.

Hmm, note 1 says employment type full_time looked up in own database. This is conflicting with note 6. As the Approver, I need to weigh. Note 6 specifically flags the discrepancy and provides the security training info.

I'll go with read, based on contractor status with basic training. Submit decision with read.
